duplicate_check.notes: No Goldfinch or Goldfinch Prime canonical platform was found in the current repository review. A full candidate audit remains required before any promotion.

notes: The first-party governance proposal moves the legacy Goldfinch protocol into recovery-only maintenance mode and winds down Goldfinch Prime. A 7 July update states that Prime investors were fully redeemed, no new deposits are accepted, and the contract was paused, while legacy V1 borrower pools remain in payment or recovery. CYA focuses on CeFi and does not prioritize DeFi lending protocols in its initial scope, so this is staged for an explicit scope and entity-boundary decision rather than forced into canonical data. Review whether Goldfinch Prime should be modeled as a historically significant institutional-yield product/platform exception, whether legacy V1 and Prime remain one platform entity, and how customer outcomes should be scoped by product.

major_event: Abra began winding down Abra Earn for United States customers in June 2023, later entered a multistate asset-return settlement, and resolved SEC charges concerning the unregistered interest-account product

duplicate_check.notes: No Abra Earn, Plutus Lending LLC, Abra Interest Account, or matching product-scoped Abra lending record was found in canonical data or consumed candidate history.

notes: Promote only as a product-scoped historical crypto interest-account record, separate from Abra's wallet, trading, institutional, and later corporate activity. The SEC states that Abra Earn launched in the United States around July 2020, reached approximately $600 million in assets, and began winding down in June 2023 with United States customers instructed to withdraw. The CSBS multistate settlement covers remaining virtual assets for United States Abra Trade customers in participating states and describes up to $82.1 million to be returned; that settlement population must not be silently treated as identical to every Abra Earn customer or as proof that all withdrawals completed. Canonical review must preserve the Plutus Lending legal-entity boundary, distinguish Earn balances from Trade accounts, separate the 2024 settlement from the SEC case and 2025 final judgment, and avoid inferring customer harm, universal repayment completion, or a recovery percentage beyond the reviewed orders.

major_event: Inlock entered an emergency shutdown on 14 November 2022 after a liquidation failure and FTX-linked asset unavailability, implemented multiple recovery paths from 2023, and completed the wind-down of customer asset-related services on 30 June 2026

duplicate_check.notes: No Inlock, INLOCK, Income Locker, inlock.io, Inlock Savings Account, or Inlock Lending Platform record was found in canonical data or consumed candidate history.

notes: Inlock is a high-value CeFi lending and savings record with a complete incident-to-wind-down arc. The operator states that deposits, withdrawals, new loans, and interest were suspended on 14 November 2022 after a liquidation failure made part of customer assets unavailable and describes FTX-linked recovery. Recovery options included migration, loss-discounted exit payout, and a Scheduled Release program beginning in April 2023. In August 2024 the operator reported that the Scheduled Release cohort had received more than 100% of the dollar value recorded at the time of loss, but customer outcomes varied by program, asset, timing, and claim treatment. The current first-party site states that all customer asset-related services ended on 30 June 2026, while historical access remains until 30 September 2026 and support until 31 December 2026. Canonical promotion must separate Savings and Loan products, operator claims from independently verified recovery, asset-value repayment from in-kind recovery, completed service wind-down from future platform decommissioning, and ILK token handling from customer asset claims.
